summary: Seychelles' official Travel Authorisation site says there are no visa requirements for any traveller visiting Seychelles. Seychelles Immigration says a Visitor's Permit is issued on arrival, initially for a stay of up to three months, to visitors who meet its criteria, and that all visitors must hold a valid Electronic Travel Authorisation before departing.

passportValidity.text: Seychelles Immigration says the passport must be valid for the period of the intended stay until arrival back in the holder's country of origin or residence. The UK Foreign Office says your passport must be valid for the duration of your stay.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: The official Travel Authorisation site says you upload a yellow fever vaccination certificate only if you are travelling from a country or region where the disease is endemic, and that you do not need one if you transit through an airport in such a region for less than 12 hours.

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for Seychelles.

onwardTicket.text: Seychelles Immigration says a valid return or onward ticket for the duration of the visit must be presented for the Visitor's Permit issued on arrival, and the official Travel Authorisation site says you can apply only after booking your airline ticket and accommodation.

proofOfFunds.text: Seychelles Immigration says a visitor must have sufficient funds for the duration of the stay, a minimum of US$150 or equivalent per day, together with a valid return or onward ticket and confirmed accommodation.

currencyLimits.text: The UK Foreign Office says that if you are taking cash with a value of 50,000 Seychellois rupees or more into Seychelles, you must declare it when you apply for your travel authorisation.

It advises using a hotel safe or safety deposit box for valuables, money and passports.

tips.text: The official Travel Authorisation site says that without one you may be denied boarding by your airline, that arriving without a pre-approved authorisation costs a penalty fee of 30 EUR at the airport, and that standard processing takes 24 hours.

The official Travel Authorisation site says that for a stay of one night or more you must submit a copy of your hotel or accommodation booking, or a letter of invitation from your host if you stay with family or friends, and that applications made with accommodation not on the Tourism Department's list of authorised establishments may be denied.

The UK Foreign Office says beaches can be safe for swimming at some times of year and dangerous at others: in general the west coast is unsafe during the north-west monsoon (around December to March), the east coast during the south-east winds season (around May to September), and beaches at the southern tip are not suitable for swimming at any time.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Seychelles?
faq.answer: No — Seychelles' official Travel Authorisation site says there are no visa requirements for any traveller visiting Seychelles. Seychelles Immigration says a Visitor's Permit is issued on arrival, initially for a stay of up to three months, and that all visitors must hold a valid Electronic Travel Authorisation before departing.

faq.question: What is the Seychelles Travel Authorisation?
faq.answer: The official site says all non-citizens travelling to Seychelles must complete the Travel Authorisation, a digital form that serves as approval for travel, applied for on the official website or in the official Seychelles e-Border app, and that travellers of all ages must comply. It lists the fee by processing speed: for adults €10 (standard, 24 hours), €30 (premium, 6 hours) or €70 (expedited, 60 minutes); for children 12 and under €10, €30 and €30; bank charges are not included. It says that without one you may be denied boarding by your airline.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Seychelles?
faq.answer: Seychelles Immigration says the Visitor's Permit is initially granted for a stay of up to three months and can be extended for successive periods of up to three months each, to a maximum total of twelve months, provided you continue to meet its criteria (a return or onward ticket, confirmed accommodation and sufficient funds).

faq.question: What do I need to show on arrival in Seychelles?
faq.answer: Seychelles Immigration says all visitors must hold a valid Electronic Travel Authorisation before departing, and that the Visitor's Permit requires a valid return or onward ticket, confirmed accommodation and sufficient funds for the stay (minimum of US$150 or equivalent per day). It says the passport must be valid for the period of the intended stay until arrival back in the holder's country of origin or residence.

faq.question: Do I need vaccinations for Seychelles?
faq.answer: The official Travel Authorisation site says you upload a yellow fever vaccination certificate only if you are travelling from a country or region where the disease is endemic, and that you do not need one if you transit through an airport in such a region for less than 12 hours.

summary.text: There are no visa requirements for any traveller visiting Seychelles.
A Visitor’s Permit is issued upon arrival in Seychelles to individuals traveling for purposes such as holiday, pleasure, business, or visiting friends and family.
The Visitor’s Permit is initially granted for a stay of up to three months.
All visitors to Seychelles must possess a valid Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) prior to departing from their country of origin.

tips.sea-conditions.text: Beaches can be safe for swimming at some times of the year and dangerous at others. In general, the west coast is unsafe during the north-west monsoon (around December to March), and the east coast is unsafe during the south-east winds season (around May to September). Beaches at the southern tip are not suitable for swimming at any time.

Medium tourism accommodation establishments (24- 50rooms) – SCR 75 per person per night.
Large tourism accommodation establishments (51 rooms onwards) – SCR 100 per person per night.
Yachts and island resorts – SCR 100 per person per night.
